input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The estimate is for a Leica M6 body with serial number 2487319 and a Summicron 50 millimeter lens with serial number 391044. The shop is Alder Camera Service on West Mason Street, and the estimate is dated April 14. The email address on Mara's file ends in Harbor Mutual dot net. I checked the address against the claim card before starting this note. The estimate is attached as a six-page PDF, and the first page gives the shop telephone number and the claim reference H M 70618.

Jonah Reed at Alder Camera Service wrote that the camera arrived in a padded case with the strap still attached. He noted a dent on the lower right corner and a loose rewind knob. The dent appears in the intake photographs from April 9. The photographs show the camera from the front, back, and both sides. Mara asked me to forward the estimate rather than call the shop because she is reviewing several equipment claims this week. The parts line is marked pending because Jonah has not confirmed whether the knob is in stock. Sales tax is listed as 8 point 25 percent, and the printed total is 397 dollars and 67 cents before any change to the parts line. The estimate says the shop will keep the camera on its intake shelf through April 22.

1. The body inspection fee is 85 dollars and covers opening the top plate and checking the shutter curtains.
2. Shutter cleaning is 140 dollars, and the shop expects to use solvent and a lint-free cloth.
3. The rewind knob replacement is 62 dollars, with availability pending.
4. Reassembly and testing labor is 110 dollars and includes a shutter speed check at one second and one eightieth of a second.
5. The estimate does not include a battery or work on the light meter.
6. The shop says any additional part or labor would need a separate estimate before it begins that work.

There is a condition that matters for the next step: if Harbor Mutual wants an independent inspection before repair begins, the camera needs to stay at Alder Camera Service, and the shop needs written notice by April 22. Otherwise, Jonah said he cannot promise that the intake shelf space will remain available. He has not said that the shop will start repairs automatically on April 23, and the estimate does not give a repair start date. Mara's email from Monday says, “Please send the current estimate and keep the camera where it is until I confirm whether we need another inspection.” I am forwarding the document only and have not asked Alder Camera Service to start work.

Jonah told me the estimate reflects what he could see without removing the stuck battery cover. He did not open the cover because he did not want to mark the metal with a tool. He said the battery compartment may need a separate assessment if Harbor Mutual later asks for meter testing. The estimate also mentions a possible two-week wait for the replacement knob but does not promise a delivery date. The shop has one earlier job ahead of this camera, and Jonah said the queue can change if a part does not arrive the same week the estimate was prepared.

The intake record gives the camera owner as North Window Studio and lists its storage address as 18 Orchard Lane, Suite 4. The claim card has the same studio name but a different mailing address at 77 Bridge Street. I used the mailing address in the email draft because that is the address shown on Mara's contact card. The email subject line reads “Claim H M 70618 camera estimate.” The attachment filename is alder estimate 0414 pdf, and the file size is 1 point 8 megabytes. The scan includes the shop's signature at the bottom of page six, and the date appears next to the signature.

I am forwarding the estimate to Mara with the intake photographs and the shop's short note about the stuck battery compartment. The photographs are separate JPG files named front 0409, back 0409, left 0409, and right 0409. I have not included the padded case photographs because those were not part of the camera estimate, and Mara only asked for the current estimate and the camera records. The email draft has no payment instruction, and it does not tell the shop to repair the camera. I will leave the camera at Alder Camera Service while the review is pending. The final page of the estimate repeats that the knob is subject to availability and gives Jonah Reed's direct number as 206 555 0148."}]
